# ghir

Search your GitHub repos, cloned or not, across every organization you belong to. Fetch once, then search offline; each hit says where it is cloned on this machine, if anywhere.

```bash
pip install ghir
ghir refresh                                   # you + your orgs, through the gh CLI
ghir search "flashcards spaced repetition"     # offline, ranked by ir
```

```default
 0.032  thorwhalen/tetrachord  /home/me/proj/tt/tetrachord
        Music education with a learner model and scheduler at the architectural centre.
 0.015  thorwhalen/rbxloop  (not cloned)
```

Requires the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh auth login`) for `refresh` only; searching never touches the network.

## The four seams

ghir is `corpus -> extraction -> ranking`, with a cache beside it. Each is one keyword argument with a working default.

| Seam                                     | Argument             | Default                                                                                       | Alternatives                                                                 |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Locations: which repos                   | `refresh(locations)` | `"@me"`: you and every org you belong to                                                      | owner logins, `"search:<github search query>"`                               |
| Extraction: what text a repo contributes | `extract=`           | `"description_and_readme"` (name, description, topics, README head)                           | `"description"`, or any `record -> str` callable                             |
| Ranking                                  | `rank=`              | `"ir"`: hybrid dense + BM25 through [ir](https://github.com/i2mint/ir), indexed incrementally | `"grep"` (query terms as word prefixes, no index, no model), or any callable |
| Cache                                    | `store=`             | one JSON file per repo under `~/.local/share/ghir/repos/`                                     | any `MutableMapping` (a `dol` store: S3, a database)                         |

`refresh` merges: fetched repos overwrite their own entries, and cached repos it did not see this time are kept. A location that fails to fetch is reported in `"failed"` and its cached repos stay.

```python
import ghir

ghir.refresh(["i2mint", "search:user:thorwhalen topic:education"])
for hit in ghir.search("audio tagging", rank="grep", include_forks=False):
    print(hit.id, hit.local_path or hit.url)
```

## Settings

Machine-specific choices go in `~/.config/ghir/config.json` (or `$GHIR_CONFIG`):

```json
{"locations": ["@me", "otosense"],
 "exclude": ["SomeClientOrg/*", "myorg/private-thing"]}
```

An owner excluded with `owner/*` is never queried. Other keys: `extract`, `local_roots` (where clones are looked for; default `$PP` or your home), `cache_dir`, `corpus_name`.

## Using it from ir

`ghir refresh` also registers the cache as the ir corpus `gh_repos` (a `records` corpus whose fetcher is `ghir:records`), so ir’s own tools see it:

```bash
ir discover gh_repos "spaced repetition"
ir discover gh_repos packages "audio tagging"    # federated with the local packages corpus
```

Why this is a separate package and not part of ir: [docs/adr/0001-where-ghir-lives.md]().

# _autosummary/ghir.cache.html.md

# ghir.cache

The repo-record cache: a `MutableMapping` from `owner/name` to a record.

Searching never goes online; it reads this cache. [`refresh()`](_autosummary/ghir.cache.html.md#ghir.cache.refresh) is the only
thing that fetches, and it *merges*: fetched records overwrite their own keys,
records not seen this time are kept (a repo outside today’s locations, or a
fetch that failed half-way, does not erase what was known). Each record carries
`fetched_at` so staleness is visible.

The store is a seam (`store=`): the default is one JSON file per repo under
[`ghir.config.DFLT_CACHE_DIR`](_autosummary/ghir.config.html.md#ghir.config.DFLT_CACHE_DIR) (a `dol` store, so an S3 or database
mapping drops in unchanged).

### Functions

| [`refresh`](_autosummary/ghir.cache.html.md#ghir.cache.refresh)([locations, store, exclude, fetch])   | Fetch the repos of `locations` and merge them into the cache.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`repo_store`](_autosummary/ghir.cache.html.md#ghir.cache.repo_store)([cache_dir])                       | The default cache: `{"owner/name": record}` over JSON files.    |

### ghir.cache.refresh(locations=None, \*, store=None, exclude=None, fetch=<function fetch_repos>, \*\*fetch_kwargs)

Fetch the repos of `locations` and merge them into the cache.

Returns counts: `{"fetched", "added", "updated", "kept"}` where `kept` is
the number of cached records this fetch did not see (and left alone), plus
`"failed"`: `{location: error}` for locations that could not be fetched
(their cached records are kept).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ghir.cache.repo_store(cache_dir=None)

The default cache: `{"owner/name": record}` over JSON files.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)


# _autosummary/ghir.config.html.md

# ghir.config

Settings for ghir: where the cache lives and which repos are in scope.

All settings have working defaults and can be overridden, in increasing order of
precedence, by a JSON file (`~/.config/ghir/config.json`, or `$GHIR_CONFIG`)
and by keyword arguments to the functions that read them. The file is the place
for machine-specific choices (extra owners, owners or repos never to fetch):

```json
{"locations": ["@me", "otosense"],
 "exclude": ["SomeClientOrg/*", "myorg/private-notes"]}
```

`"@me"` expands to the authenticated GitHub user plus every organization they
belong to (see [`ghir.fetch.my_owners()`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.my_owners)).

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_CACHE_DIR`](_autosummary/ghir.config.html.md#ghir.config.DFLT_CACHE_DIR)   | Where fetched repo records are cached (one JSON file per `owner/name`).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_CONFIG_PATH`](_autosummary/ghir.config.html.md#ghir.config.DFLT_CONFIG_PATH) | The optional user settings file.                                          |
| [`DFLT_CORPUS_NAME`](_autosummary/ghir.config.html.md#ghir.config.DFLT_CORPUS_NAME) | The ir corpus name the default records are registered under.              |

### Functions

| [`settings`](_autosummary/ghir.config.html.md#ghir.config.settings)([path])   | The effective settings: defaults, then the config file, then `overrides`.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ghir.config.DFLT_CACHE_DIR *= PosixPath('/home/runner/.local/share/ghir/repos')*

Where fetched repo records are cached (one JSON file per `owner/name`).

### ghir.config.DFLT_CONFIG_PATH *= PosixPath('/home/runner/.config/ghir/config.json')*

The optional user settings file.

### ghir.config.DFLT_CORPUS_NAME *= 'gh_repos'*

The ir corpus name the default records are registered under.

### ghir.config.settings(path=None, \*\*overrides)

The effective settings: defaults, then the config file, then `overrides`.

```pycon
>>> s = settings(path="/nonexistent/ghir.json", exclude=["acme/*"])
>>> s["exclude"], s["locations"]
(['acme/*'], ['@me'])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# ghir.extract

Extraction: what text each cached repo contributes to the search.

An extractor is a function `record -> str`. `extractors` names the
built-in ones; any callable works wherever an extractor is accepted. The text
returned is what gets indexed and ranked, so it decides what a query can match.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_README_CHARS`](_autosummary/ghir.extract.html.md#ghir.extract.DFLT_README_CHARS)   | README characters kept by the default extractor (READMEs can be huge, and their opening says what the repo is).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`resolve_extractor`](_autosummary/ghir.extract.html.md#ghir.extract.resolve_extractor)(extract)                      | An extractor from its name in `extractors`, or a callable as is.      |

### ghir.extract.DFLT_README_CHARS *= 6000*

README characters kept by the default extractor (READMEs can be huge, and
their opening says what the repo is).

Name, description and topics.

# _autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md

# ghir.fetch

Fetching repo records from GitHub, through the `gh` CLI’s GraphQL access.

One GraphQL page returns up to `DFLT_PAGE_SIZE` repos *with* their README
text, so a whole organization costs a handful of calls rather than one per repo.

The transport is a seam: every function takes `graphql=`, a callable
`(query, variables) -> dict`. The default shells out to `gh api graphql`
(so authentication is whatever `gh auth login` set up); tests pass a fake.

A *location* is one of:

- an owner login (`"i2mint"`): every repo of that user or organization;
- `"@me"`: the authenticated user and every organization they belong to;
- `"search:<query>"`: the repos a GitHub search returns
  (`"search:user:thorwhalen topic:education"`).

### Module Attributes

| [`MIN_PAGE_SIZE`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.MIN_PAGE_SIZE)   | On a gateway error (README blobs make pages slow), the page size is halved down to this before the error is let through.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`README_NAMES`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.README_NAMES)    | README file names tried, in order, at the default branch's root.                                                           |

### Functions

| [`expand_locations`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.expand_locations)(locations, \*[, owners])          | Replace `"@me"` by the user's owners; keep order, drop duplicates.      |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`fetch_location`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.fetch_location)(location, \*[, graphql, page_size]) | Yield normalized repo records for one owner login or `search:` spec.    |
| [`fetch_repos`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.fetch_repos)(locations, \*[, exclude, ...])         | Yield repo records over all `locations`, skipping excluded repos.       |
| [`gh_api`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.gh_api)(path)                                       | `gh api <path>` (REST), JSON-decoded.                                   |
| [`gh_graphql`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.gh_graphql)(query, variables)                       | Run a GraphQL query through `gh api graphql` and return its `data`.     |
| [`is_excluded`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.is_excluded)(repo_id, exclude)                      | Whether `owner/name` matches any fnmatch pattern of `exclude`.          |
| [`my_owners`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.my_owners)(\*[, rest])                              | The authenticated user's login followed by their organizations' logins. |
| [`normalize_repo`](_autosummary/ghir.fetch.html.md#ghir.fetch.normalize_repo)(node)                               | Flatten one GraphQL repository node into a JSON-friendly record.        |

### ghir.fetch.MIN_PAGE_SIZE *= 3*

On a gateway error (README blobs make pages slow), the page size is halved
down to this before the error is let through.

### ghir.fetch.README_NAMES *= ('README.md', 'readme.md', 'README.rst', 'README', 'README.txt')*

README file names tried, in order, at the default branch’s root.

### ghir.fetch.expand_locations(locations, \*, owners=<function my_owners>)

Replace `"@me"` by the user’s owners; keep order, drop duplicates.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### ghir.fetch.fetch_location(location, \*, graphql=<function gh_graphql>, page_size=25)

Yield normalized repo records for one owner login or `search:` spec.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

A location whose fetch fails is passed to `on_error(location, error)` and

Flatten one GraphQL repository node into a JSON-friendly record.

```pycon
>>> normalize_repo({"nameWithOwner": "a/b", "name": "b",

...     "repositoryTopics": {"nodes": [{"topic": {"name": "x"}}]},
...     "readme0": None, "readme1": {"text": "hi"}})["readme"]
'hi'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/ghir.html.md

# ghir

Search your GitHub repos, cloned or not, as an `ir` corpus.

Four seams, each a keyword argument with a working default:

- **locations** ([`refresh()`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.refresh)): owner logins, `"@me"` (you and your orgs),
  or `"search:<github query>"`.
- **extraction** (`extract=`): what text a repo contributes; default
  description + topics + README head ([`ghir.extract`](_autosummary/ghir.extract.html.md#module-ghir.extract)).
- **ranking** (`rank=`): `"ir"` (default, hybrid dense + BM25) or `"grep"`.
- **cache** (`store=`): a `MutableMapping`; [`refresh()`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.refresh) merges into it,
  [`search()`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.search) only reads it (offline).

```pycon
>>> import ghir
>>> ghir.refresh()
>>> for hit in ghir.search("flashcards spaced repetition"):
...     print(hit.id, hit.local_path)
```

### Functions

| [`fetch_repos`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.fetch_repos)(locations, \*[, exclude, ...])         | Yield repo records over all `locations`, skipping excluded repos.             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`grep_rank`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.grep_rank)(query, docs, \*[, k])                    | Fraction of query terms (as word prefixes) found in each repo's text.         |
| [`ir_rank`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.ir_rank)(query, docs, \*[, k, mode, embedder, ...]) | Rank with `ir`: build (incrementally) then `ir.search`.                       |
| [`local_clones`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.local_clones)(roots, \*[, max_depth])               | `{"owner/name" (lowercased): path}` for git checkouts under `roots`.          |
| [`records`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.records)()                                          | The default records, as a zero-argument fetcher for ir's registry.            |
| [`refresh`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.refresh)([locations, store, exclude, fetch])        | Fetch the repos of `locations` and merge them into the cache.                 |
| [`register_corpus`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.register_corpus)([name])                            | Register the cache as an ir corpus, so `ir discover <name> ...` works.        |
| [`repo_store`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.repo_store)([cache_dir])                            | The default cache: `{"owner/name": record}` over JSON files.                  |
| [`search`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.search)(query, \*[, k, rank, extract, store, ...])  | Rank cached repos for `query`; each hit says where it is cloned, if anywhere. |
| [`settings`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.settings)([path])                                   | The effective settings: defaults, then the config file, then `overrides`.     |

### Classes

| [`RepoHit`](_autosummary/ghir.html.md#ghir.RepoHit)(id, score, description, url[, ...])   | One search result: a repo, its score, and where it is cloned (if it is).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

One search result: a repo, its score, and where it is cloned (if it is).

### ghir.fetch_repos(locations, \*, exclude=(), graphql=<function gh_graphql>, owners=<function my_owners>, on_error=None)

Yield repo records over all `locations`, skipping excluded repos.

A location whose fetch fails is passed to `on_error(location, error)` and
skipped, or, when `on_error` is None, the error propagates.

An owner pattern in `exclude` (`"Acme/*"`) also stops that owner from
being queried at all, so nothing of it is fetched.

Fetch the repos of `locations` and merge them into the cache.

Returns counts: `{"fetched", "added", "updated", "kept"}` where `kept` is

# _autosummary/ghir.local.html.md

# ghir.local

Which GitHub repos are cloned on this machine, and where.

Scans root directories a few levels deep for git checkouts and reads each one’s
`origin` remote, giving `{"owner/name": local_path}`. Plain file reads, no
`git` subprocess, so a scan of a few hundred checkouts takes well under a second.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_MAX_DEPTH`](_autosummary/ghir.local.html.md#ghir.local.DFLT_MAX_DEPTH)   | How many directory levels below each root to look for checkouts.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

### ghir.local.DFLT_MAX_DEPTH *= 3*

How many directory levels below each root to look for checkouts.

### ghir.local.local_clones(roots, , max_depth=3)

`{"owner/name" (lowercased): path}` for git checkouts under `roots`.

### ghir.local.origin_repo_id(config_text)

The `owner/name` of the first GitHub remote in a `.git/config`.

```pycon
>>> origin_repo_id('[remote "origin"]\n\turl = git@github.com:i2mint/ir.git\n')
'i2mint/ir'
>>> origin_repo_id('url = https://github.com/thorwhalen/learny\n')
'thorwhalen/learny'
```

* **Return type:**
